decisions.reason: CCA affects calculated equity returns, but the availability-payment sizing thresholds and criteria are already independently established and remain unchanged.
The CCA decision does not change the confirmed debt/equity ratio, financing rate, tranche structure, or financing-refinement trigger.
Applying asset-specific CCA classes uses asset categories but does not change capex values, assumption basis, or required shared-program capex line items.
Tax depreciation and CCA do not alter the confirmed operating-cost range, source, or Appendix applicability.
The CCA methodology does not change the eight-site count, selected Business Case site list, or site-level configuration basis.
CCA may influence scenario outputs, but it does not change the required user-funded and PPP scenarios or the availability-payment justification requirement.
The tax calculation changes within the model, but the candidate's integrated three-statement structure and financial-engine basis remain valid unchanged.
The source does not add CCA or tax as a sensitivity variable or otherwise alter the existing sensitivity-analysis specification.
The general obligation to annotate assumptions and their sources already applies; the CCA decision does not change that traceability policy.
The CCA methodology does not change the requirement to verify source data or the designated roles of the project brief, attachments, and demand analysis.
The tax and depreciation decision does not change revenue streams, pricing assumptions, or revenue-assumption documentation.
Applying Canadian CCA classes is consistent with, but does not modify, the established CAD currency and 2026 price base year.
